name: Bergamot
description: A green, slightly bitter citrus from southern Italy, brighter and more floral than lemon. It's the classic sparkling opening of colognes and Earl Grey tea.

name: Lemon
description: Sharp, zesty and clean, like a freshly cut lemon peel. It lifts a perfume instantly but fades fast, so it lives in the opening.

name: Mandarin Orange
description: Sweeter and juicier than lemon, with a soft, almost candied orange glow. Smells cheerful and sunny rather than sharp.

name: Orange
description: Juicy, sweet orange peel - like peeling a ripe orange. Friendly and fruity, it brightens the top of a scent.

name: Grapefruit
description: Tangy and a little bitter, with a sulfurous, juicy edge that reads fresh and modern. Popular in sporty and unisex scents.

name: Lime
description: Tart, green and zingy, like a mojito garnish. Adds a sharp, tropical sparkle.

name: Yuzu
description: A Japanese citrus that smells like a mix of grapefruit, mandarin and lime, with a floral twist. Crisp, airy and elegant.

name: Neroli
description: Oil from bitter-orange blossoms: fresh, honeyed and slightly green. Sits between citrus and floral and smells clean and luminous.

name: Petitgrain
description: Distilled from the leaves and twigs of the bitter-orange tree. Woody-green and a bit bitter, like neroli's outdoorsy sibling.

name: Rose
description: The queen of florals: velvety, rich and slightly fruity or spicy depending on the variety. Can feel romantic and classic or dark and jammy.

name: Jasmine
description: A heady white flower that's sweet, creamy and a little animalic thanks to a natural molecule called indole. Sensual and full-bodied.

name: Tuberose
description: A buttery, intoxicating white flower, creamy and almost rubbery-sweet. One of the loudest, most glamorous florals in perfumery.

name: Ylang-Ylang
description: A tropical flower with a custardy, banana-like sweetness. Rich and sunny, often used to make florals feel lush.

name: Iris
description: Made from the dried root, not the flower: powdery, earthy and cool, like lipstick or fine cosmetic powder. One of the most expensive materials in perfumery.

name: Violet
description: Soft, powdery and sweet, a bit like old-fashioned violet candies. Gentle and slightly nostalgic.

name: Violet Leaf
description: Not floral at all: a sharp, watery green that smells like crushed leaves or cucumber skin. Adds a cool, modern freshness.

name: Lavender
description: Herbal, clean and slightly sweet, the backbone of many classic men's 'fougère' scents. Calming and fresh, with a hint of camphor.

name: Lily of the Valley
description: Fresh, dewy and green-floral, like spring in a bottle. The flower gives no oil, so its scent is recreated with synthetic molecules.

name: Orange Blossom
description: Sweet, honeyed and bright, warmer and more sensual than neroli (they come from the same flower). Smells like sunshine and clean skin.

name: Osmanthus
description: A tiny Chinese blossom that smells of ripe apricots, leather and tea. Fruity-floral with a suede-like softness.

name: Gardenia
description: A creamy white flower with green, mushroomy facets. Lush and sweet, often recreated from other florals.

name: Magnolia
description: Light, lemony and creamy, a fresher and brighter white floral. Feels airy and elegant.

name: Peony
description: Fresh, pink and slightly rosy with a watery touch. Youthful and pretty, without the heaviness of rose.

name: Geranium
description: Rosy and minty-green at once, with a metallic edge. Common in men's fragrances to add a fresh floral heart.

name: Immortelle
description: A Mediterranean flower that smells of honey, curry leaves, hay and maple syrup. Warm, sun-baked and slightly salty.

name: Heliotrope
description: A powdery flower that smells of almond, vanilla and Play-Doh. Soft, sweet and comforting.

name: Mimosa
description: Fluffy yellow blossoms with a powdery, honeyed scent and a hint of cucumber. Gentle and sunny.

name: Saffron
description: A rare spice with a leathery, metallic, honeyed smell. Adds warmth and an exotic, slightly medicinal glow.

name: Pink Pepper
description: Not true pepper: a rosy, fizzy berry with a sparkling, slightly fruity spice. Gives openings a playful lift.

name: Pepper
description: Dry, sharp and woody, like freshly cracked peppercorns. Adds a crisp bite and energy.

name: Sichuan Pepper
description: Citrusy and tingling, more lemony than black pepper. Brings a bright, electric spice.

name: Cardamom
description: Fresh, eucalyptus-like and gently sweet, like chai. Cool and warm at the same time.

name: Cinnamon
description: Warm, sweet and woody, like holiday baking. Cozy and a little fiery.

name: Clove
description: Hot, medicinal and sweet, like a dentist's office crossed with mulled wine. Strong and warming.

name: Nutmeg
description: Warm, soft and slightly woody spice. Rounds out fresh or woody blends with a comforting touch.

name: Ginger
description: Zesty, juicy and spicy-fresh, like fresh-cut ginger root. Bright rather than warm.

name: Elemi
description: A tree resin that smells peppery, lemony and incense-like. Fresh and resinous at once.

name: Sandalwood
description: Creamy, milky and smooth wood with a soft, skin-like warmth. One of the most comforting base notes.

name: Cedar
description: Dry, clean and pencil-shaving woody. Gives structure and a crisp backbone to a scent.

name: Vetiver
description: A grass root that smells smoky, earthy and green, like damp soil and roots. Elegant, dry and long-lasting.

name: Patchouli
description: Earthy, dark and slightly chocolatey, from a dried leaf. Modern versions are cleaner; vintage ones feel more hippie and damp.

name: Oud
description: A dark resin formed in infected agarwood trees: smoky, leathery, medicinal and animalic. Prized and expensive, often recreated synthetically.

name: Akigalawood
description: A modern ingredient made by upcycling patchouli with enzymes. Smells woody and peppery with a soft oud-like and spicy facet.

name: Guaiac Wood
description: Smoky, warm and slightly sweet wood, like a campfire with a hint of tar. Adds depth and dryness.

name: Cashmeran
description: A synthetic that smells like soft wool, warm skin and musky wood. Cozy and velvety.

name: Iso E Super
description: A transparent synthetic wood with a velvety, cedar-like glow. Some people can barely smell it, but it makes perfumes feel radiant on skin.

name: Cypress
description: Resinous, green and slightly smoky, like a pine forest. Fresh and outdoorsy.

name: Birch
description: Smoky and tarry, the classic material used to create leather accords. Dark and dramatic.

name: Vanilla
description: Sweet, creamy and comforting, sometimes boozy or smoky. Warms and softens almost any base.

name: Tonka Bean
description: Smells like vanilla, almond and fresh hay mixed together, thanks to a molecule called coumarin. Warm, sweet and a bit nutty.

name: Benzoin
description: A balsamic tree resin with a vanilla-caramel sweetness. Cozy and slightly powdery.

name: Labdanum
description: A sticky resin from the rockrose shrub: leathery, ambery and rich. The heart of many 'amber' accords.

name: Amber
description: Not a single ingredient but a warm blend, usually labdanum, vanilla and benzoin. Smells golden, resinous and sweet.

name: Ambroxan
description: A synthetic inspired by ambergris: salty, woody, musky and very long-lasting. The signature trail of many modern men's scents.

name: Ambergris
description: A rare material formed in sperm whales and aged by the sea: salty, marine, sweet and skin-like. Today it's almost always recreated synthetically.

name: Incense
description: Smoky, lemony and resinous, like a church or temple. Gives a mystical, airy depth.

name: Myrrh
description: A bitter, balsamic resin with a medicinal, slightly mushroomy depth. Darker and earthier than frankincense.

name: Honey
description: Sweet, waxy and slightly animalic, sometimes even a bit sweaty. Adds warmth and richness.

name: Caramel
description: Sugary, buttery and burnt-sweet. A classic note of dessert-like 'gourmand' perfumes.

name: Coffee
description: Roasted, bitter and dark, like fresh espresso. Adds depth to sweet and woody scents.

name: Cocoa
description: Dry, powdery and bittersweet, like cocoa powder rather than milk chocolate. Cozy and grown-up.

name: Praline
description: Toasted nuts in caramelized sugar. Very sweet and edible.

name: Almond
description: Marzipan-like and cherry-ish, sweet and slightly bitter. Soft and nostalgic.

name: Rum
description: Boozy, molasses-sweet and warm. Gives a cozy, adult sweetness.

name: Tobacco
description: Dried tobacco leaf, not cigarette smoke: sweet, hay-like, honeyed and a little fruity. Warm and gentlemanly.

name: Musk
description: Soft, clean and skin-like, like fresh laundry or warm skin. Today it's always synthetic, and it makes a perfume last and feel intimate.

name: Leather
description: An accord that recreates tanned leather: smoky, animalic and a little sweet. Can feel rugged or luxurious.

name: Suede
description: A softer, plusher take on leather: powdery, velvety and gentle. Feels like brushing a suede glove.

name: Civet
description: An animalic note that's musky and fecal in isolation but adds sensual warmth in tiny doses. Now almost always synthetic.

name: Castoreum
description: Leathery, smoky and birch-like animalic note, now recreated synthetically. Adds depth to leather and amber scents.

name: Ozone
description: The smell of fresh air before or after a thunderstorm: crisp, clean and slightly metallic. Made with synthetic molecules to suggest open air and sky.

name: Sea Notes
description: A salty, breezy accord that evokes the seaside, often built on the molecule Calone. Fresh, airy and a bit watery.

name: Calone
description: A synthetic that smells like sea breeze crossed with watermelon. It defined the 'aquatic' fragrances of the 1990s.

name: Mineral Notes
description: An abstract accord suggesting wet stone, chalk or flint. Cool, dry and slightly metallic, like rocks after rain.

name: Aldehydes
description: Synthetic molecules that smell fizzy, soapy and waxy, like champagne bubbles or ironed linen. Famous for making Chanel No. 5 sparkle.

name: Petrichor
description: The earthy smell of rain on dry ground. Often built with geosmin-like notes for a damp, soil-like freshness.

name: Mint
description: Cool, sharp and refreshing. Gives an icy, clean lift to the opening.

name: Basil
description: Green, peppery and slightly anise-like herb. Fresh and Mediterranean.

name: Rosemary
description: Herbal, piney and camphorous. Classic in colognes for a clean, invigorating feel.

name: Sage
description: Herbal and musky, with a slightly sweet, tea-like warmth. Clary sage especially adds a soft, ambery hum.

name: Tea
description: Green tea is fresh, light and slightly bitter; black tea is smoky and tannic. Both feel calm and refined.

name: Fig
description: Milky, green and woody, like the leaves and sap of a fig tree. Often more leafy than fruity.

name: Galbanum
description: An intensely bitter, sharp green resin, like snapped stems. Very strong, used in small doses for a crisp edge.

name: Grass
description: Fresh-cut lawn: sharp, green and juicy. Feels outdoorsy and springlike.

name: Apple
description: Crisp and juicy, from tart green to sweet red. Adds a fresh, playful sweetness.

name: Pear
description: Juicy, watery and gently sweet. Light and youthful.

name: Peach
description: Fuzzy, ripe and creamy-sweet. Can feel innocent or lusciously sensual.

name: Blackcurrant
description: Tart, jammy and a little catty-green. Adds a vibrant, dark fruitiness.

name: Raspberry
description: Sweet-tart and jammy berry. Playful and bright.

name: Pineapple
description: Tropical, sharp and juicy-sweet. Famous in smoky-fruity men's scents.

name: Coconut
description: Creamy, milky and tropical, like sunscreen and summer. Soft and warm.

name: Cherry
description: Sweet, almond-tinged and sometimes boozy. Juicy and flirtatious.

name: Plum
description: Dark, jammy and wine-like. Adds richness to rose and amber scents.

name: Oakmoss
description: A lichen that grows on oak bark: damp, inky and forest-floor green. It's the backbone of classic chypre perfumes, now used in tiny, regulated amounts.

name: Cumin
description: A warm, earthy spice with a sweaty, skin-like edge. In small doses it makes a scent feel sensual and lived-in.

name: Coriander
description: The seed smells lemony, peppery and slightly woody. It adds a bright, airy spice to openings.

name: Juniper
description: Crisp, piney and resinous, the same berry that flavours gin. It brings a cold, fresh sharpness.

name: Gin
description: An accord built around juniper and botanicals: cool, boozy and herbal, like a gin and tonic.

name: Cypriol
description: The root of an Indian grass, also called nagarmotha. Smoky, earthy and leathery, often used to suggest oud.

name: Opoponax
description: Also called sweet myrrh: a warm, honeyed, balsamic resin. Softer and sweeter than regular myrrh.

name: Cistus
description: The rockrose shrub, source of labdanum. Smells resinous, ambery and a little leathery and animalic.

name: Styrax
description: A sticky tree balsam with a smoky, leathery-sweet, slightly cinnamon-like smell. Adds dark warmth.

name: Peru Balsam
description: A thick resin that smells of vanilla, cinnamon and caramel. Rich, cosy and sweet.

name: Carnation
description: A spicy flower that smells strongly of clove. Old-fashioned and peppery-floral.

name: Freesia
description: Light, peppery and fresh, like a clean bouquet. A common note in bright, modern florals.

name: Lily
description: Heady and creamy with a green, slightly spicy edge. Big and luminous.

name: Linden Blossom
description: The flower of the lime (linden) tree: honeyed, green and gently citrusy, like a warm summer evening.

name: Hyacinth
description: Green, cool and intensely floral, like a spring bulb in bloom. Slightly earthy and watery.

name: Narcissus
description: Rich, hay-like and a bit animalic, with honeyed green tones. Daffodils smell similar but lighter.

name: Tiare
description: The Tahitian gardenia: creamy, coconut-tinged and sunny. Smells like a tropical holiday.

name: Orchid
description: An imaginary accord, since most orchids barely smell: usually soft, creamy and slightly vanilla-like.

name: Hedione
description: A synthetic jasmine molecule that smells airy, lemony and transparent. It makes perfumes feel radiant and diffusive.

name: Rhubarb
description: Tart, crunchy and slightly fruity-green, like a freshly snapped stalk. Adds a sparkling, sour freshness.

name: Green Notes
description: A general term for fresh, leafy, just-cut smells. Crisp and natural.

name: Papyrus
description: Dry, smoky and woody, related to cypriol. Feels earthy and a little ancient.

name: Palo Santo
description: A South American 'holy wood' that smells sweet, smoky and minty-citrus when burned.

name: Oak
description: Dry, toasty wood, sometimes like a whisky barrel. Adds a sturdy, warm backbone.

name: Woody Notes
description: A general term for dry, warm wood smells when a source doesn't name a specific wood.

name: Fir
description: Fir needles and resin: fresh, balsamic and a bit sweet, like a Christmas tree.

name: Pine
description: Sharp, resinous and green, like a walk through a pine forest.

name: Amberwood
description: A family of modern synthetics that smell dry, woody and ambery with a slightly salty glow. Very long-lasting.

name: Georgywood
description: A modern synthetic wood note: smooth, dry and slightly ambery, similar in feel to Iso E Super.

name: Mystikal
description: A modern synthetic with a resinous, incense-like warmth. Used to give a mysterious, ambery depth.

name: Safraleine
description: A synthetic saffron note: leathery, slightly metallic and warm. Smells like saffron with a darker edge.

name: Ambrette
description: Seeds of a hibiscus plant that smell musky, pear-like and slightly winey. A natural alternative to animal musk.

name: Anise
description: Sweet, liquorice-like spice, as in star anise or fennel. Adds a cool, candied lift.

name: Liquorice
description: Sweet, dark and slightly salty, like black liquorice. Adds a chewy, gourmand depth.

name: Turmeric
description: Earthy, warm and slightly woody-bitter, like the golden spice root. Gives a dry, sunny spice.

name: Sesame
description: Toasty, nutty and warm, like toasted sesame seeds. A cosy, slightly savoury touch.

name: Hazelnut
description: Roasted, buttery nuttiness. Cosy and sweet, often paired with vanilla or coffee.

name: Maté
description: The South American tea: green, hay-like and slightly smoky. Grassy and comforting.

name: Paprika
description: Warm, slightly sweet and smoky pepper. Unusual in perfume, it adds a dry, glowing spice.

name: Fenugreek
description: Smells like maple syrup and curry at once. Warm, sweet and savoury.

name: Costus
description: A root with a waxy, hairy, animalic smell, sometimes compared to unwashed hair. Adds sensual depth in small doses.

name: Lavandin
description: A hybrid of lavender that's sharper and more camphorous. Fresh and herbal.

name: Myrtle
description: A Mediterranean shrub: fresh, green and slightly medicinal, between eucalyptus and bay leaf.

name: Mace
description: The lacy outer layer of nutmeg: warm, peppery and a little sharper than nutmeg itself.

name: Caraway
description: Warm, slightly minty and anise-like seed, as in rye bread. Close cousin of cumin.

name: Pimento
description: Allspice: smells like a mix of clove, cinnamon and pepper. Warm and festive.

name: Angelica
description: A root with a musky, earthy and slightly peppery-green smell. Adds an unusual, herbal depth.

name: Artemisia
description: Wormwood and its relatives: bitter, herbal and slightly medicinal. Fresh and green.

name: Melon
description: Juicy, watery and sweet. A hallmark of fresh, aquatic perfumes from the 1990s.

name: Blackberry
description: Dark, tart and jammy berry. Juicy with a hint of green leaf.

name: Nectarine
description: Juicy and sunny like peach, but a little brighter and less fuzzy.

name: Prunol
description: An accord that recreates dried plum: dark, jammy and slightly boozy.

name: Cucumber
description: Cool, watery and green, like a freshly sliced cucumber. Made with aroma-chemicals, it adds a crisp, dewy freshness to openings.

name: Milk
description: A soft, creamy, slightly sweet note that smells like warm milk. It's built from lactones and other creamy molecules, since milk itself can't be distilled.

name: Lactones
description: Aroma-chemicals with a creamy, milky smell, often with a peach or coconut edge. They give gourmand perfumes their smooth, dairy-like softness.

name: Cream
description: A rich, buttery, whipped-cream note that makes a perfume feel soft and dessert-like.

name: Brown Sugar
description: A warm, caramel-edged sweetness, darker and more molasses-like than white sugar.

name: Bamboo
description: A light, green, slightly watery note evoking fresh bamboo stalks and leaves. It's a fantasy accord, since bamboo has very little scent of its own.

name: Matcha
description: Powdered Japanese green tea: grassy, slightly bitter and creamy, greener and more vegetal than brewed tea.

name: Rice
description: A soft, starchy, gently sweet note like steamed rice. Jasmine rice adds a nutty, popcorn-like aroma.

name: Lotus
description: A clean, watery, gently powdery floral evoking lotus blooms on still water. Usually a recreated accord rather than a real extract.

name: Pandan
description: A Southeast Asian leaf with a sweet, grassy, vanilla-and-rice-like smell, used in desserts across Vietnam and the region.

name: Corn
description: A sweet, buttery, slightly toasted note like fresh sweet corn or corn custard.

name: Cognac
description: A boozy note of aged grape brandy: warm, fruity, woody and a little sweet.

name: Tonalide
description: A synthetic musk with a soft, sweet, powdery and slightly woody smell, used to give a clean, cosy trail.

name: Mango
description: Juicy, tropical and sweet, with a slightly resinous, green edge from the mango skin.

name: Cannabis
description: A green, herbal, slightly skunky and resinous note recreating the smell of hemp leaves, not the drug's effects.

name: Guava
description: A tropical fruit with a sweet, musky, slightly floral smell. Guava leaf is greener and more herbal.

name: Watermelon
description: Light, juicy and watery, the smell of fresh watermelon flesh. Often made with calone-like aroma-chemicals.

name: Ginseng
description: A root with an earthy, slightly bitter and woody smell, bringing a dry, rooty freshness.

name: Parsley
description: A sharp, green, slightly peppery herb note, rare in perfume, that adds a savoury freshness.

name: Eucalyptus
description: Cool, camphorous and medicinal, like a fresh eucalyptus leaf crushed between your fingers.

name: Citrus Notes
description: A general blend of citrus fruits (lemon, orange, bergamot and the like) used for a bright, zesty opening.

name: Hay
description: Warm, dry and sweet, like sun-dried grass. Hay absolute gets much of its smell from coumarin.

name: Honeysuckle
description: A sweet, nectar-like white flower with a honeyed, slightly green scent.

name: Moss
description: A damp, green, earthy forest-floor note. In perfume it usually means oakmoss or tree moss, or a substitute for them.

name: White Flowers
description: A blend of creamy white blossoms such as jasmine, tuberose and orange blossom, used for a soft, luminous floral feel.

name: Red Berries
description: A juicy, slightly tart blend of berries such as raspberry, strawberry and redcurrant.

name: Strawberry
description: Sweet, jammy and juicy, the smell of ripe strawberries.

name: Lychee
description: A tropical fruit with a sweet, rosy, slightly watery scent. It pairs naturally with rose.

name: Citron
description: An old, thick-skinned citrus fruit with a dry, zesty, less juicy smell than lemon.

name: Verbena
description: A herb with a bright, lemony, slightly green scent, fresher and softer than lemon itself.

name: Smoke
description: A dry, smoky note like a wood fire or smouldering incense, often from birch tar or cade.

name: Spices
description: A general blend of warm kitchen spices such as cinnamon, clove and nutmeg.

name: Orcanox
description: A modern aroma-chemical with a dry, woody-amber smell close to ambergris, used to add warmth and lasting power.

name: Davana
description: An Indian herb whose oil smells boozy, fruity and a little like dried apricots.

name: Pittosporum
description: A shrub with small, sweet-smelling flowers, like orange blossom with a honeyed edge.

name: Maltol
description: An aroma-chemical that smells of caramelised sugar and candy floss, giving a sweet, baked feel.

name: Datura
description: A trumpet-shaped night flower with a heady, creamy white-floral scent, close to tuberose.

name: Resins
description: Thick tree saps such as benzoin, labdanum and myrrh: warm, balsamic and slightly sweet.

name: Amyris
description: A Caribbean wood with a soft, slightly smoky, sandalwood-like smell, sometimes called West Indian sandalwood.

name: Marjoram
description: A herb close to oregano, warm, sweet and slightly camphorous.

name: Thyme
description: A Mediterranean herb with a warm, dry, slightly medicinal smell.

name: Fennel
description: A herb with a sweet, aniseed-like smell, greener and lighter than anise.

name: Cascarilla
description: The bark of a Caribbean shrub with a warm, peppery, slightly woody smell.

name: Ivy
description: A dark, crisp green-leaf note, a little bitter, like crushed ivy leaves.

name: Ambrettolide
description: A synthetic musk that smells soft, fruity and powdery, similar to ambrette seed.

name: Bayberry
description: The myrica shrub, with a resinous, herbal, slightly spicy smell like bay leaves.

name: Marigold
description: Tagetes, with a green, fruity, slightly bitter scent reminiscent of crushed leaves and apple.

name: Four O'Clock Flower
description: Mirabilis jalapa, a flower that opens late in the afternoon with a sweet, delicate scent.

name: Spun Sugar
description: The airy sweetness of candy floss, sugary and lightly caramelised.

name: Chestnut
description: Roasted chestnuts: nutty, warm, slightly sweet and smoky.

name: Cade
description: An oil from juniper wood with a strongly smoky, tarry smell, like a campfire.

name: Carrot Seed
description: An earthy, woody, slightly sweet oil whose smell is close to orris (iris root).

name: Nettle
description: A green, herbal, slightly metallic note evoking fresh nettle leaves.

name: Peach Blossom
description: A light, sweet floral with a soft hint of peach fruit.

name: Tomato Leaf
description: Sharp, green and slightly bitter, the smell of rubbing a tomato plant's leaves.

name: Paradisone
description: A purer, stronger form of Hedione: an aroma-chemical with an airy, radiant jasmine-like freshness that makes a perfume feel brighter and more transparent.

name: Cetalox
description: A brand of Ambroxide, the molecule behind ambergris: dry, woody, slightly salty and skin-like, with great lasting power.

name: Cachalox
description: An aroma-chemical recreating the warm, animalic, salty smell of natural ambergris (the name nods to the sperm whale, 'cachalot').

name: Muscenone
description: A modern musk molecule with a rich, warm, slightly animalic smell, close to natural musk.

name: Muscone
description: The main scent molecule of natural deer musk, now made synthetically: warm, soft, animalic and skin-like.

name: Exaltolide
description: A clean, smooth musk molecule with a soft, slightly sweet, powdery character. One of the most used musks in fine fragrance.

name: Exaltone
description: A musk molecule with a warm, rich, animalic edge, like a velvety skin scent.

name: Habanolide
description: A clean, metallic-fresh musk that smells like freshly ironed laundry.

name: Helvetolide
description: A fruity, pear-like musk that gives a soft, clean, slightly sweet trail.

name: Dreamwood
description: A sustainable sandalwood substitute with a creamy, milky, rich wood smell.

name: Clearwood
description: A clean, bright, patchouli-like wood made by fermentation, without patchouli's earthy, camphor side.

name: Vulcanolide
description: A woody, mineral, slightly smoky musk with a dry, sunbaked-rock feel.

name: Limbanol
description: A woody aroma-chemical with a dry, ambery, cedar-like smell.

name: Woodleather
description: A woody-leathery accord with the dry, smoky smell of soft leather and wood.

name: Cascalone
description: A marine molecule related to Calone, smelling of sea air, fresh water and a hint of melon.

name: Irone
description: The molecule that gives iris root (orris) its powdery, violet-like, slightly woody smell.

name: Z11
description: A woody-amber aroma-chemical with a dry, warm, slightly velvety smell, used to add depth and lasting power.

name: Chamomile
description: A herbal, apple-like, slightly honeyed scent, calm and soothing like chamomile tea.

name: Gurjun Balsam
description: A resin from Asian dipterocarp trees, woody and slightly earthy, often used to soften and fix other notes.

name: Hawthorn
description: A spring blossom with an almond-like, slightly powdery and honeyed smell.

name: Liatris
description: Also called deer's tongue: a plant with a hay-like, vanilla-tinged, coumarin-rich smell.

name: White Woods
description: A clean, pale, smooth woody accord, soft and dry rather than smoky or dark.

name: Sun-Warmed Woods
description: A warm, dry woody accord evoking wood baking in the sun.

name: Cyclamen
description: A delicate, watery, slightly green floral, airy and fresh rather than heady.

name: Pomelo
description: The largest citrus fruit, smelling like a softer, sweeter, less bitter grapefruit.

name: Buchu
description: A South African herb with a sharp, minty-fruity smell, often compared to blackcurrant.

name: Rosewood
description: A smooth, slightly rosy and spicy wood. Brazilian rosewood is now protected, so it's usually recreated.

name: Crème Brûlée
description: Vanilla custard under a crackling caramelised sugar crust: creamy, eggy and burnt-sweet.

name: Tulip
description: Real tulips barely smell, so the note is an accord: green, fresh and lightly floral, like crisp petals and stems.

name: Naseberry
description: Also called sapodilla: a tropical fruit with a sweet, malty, pear-and-brown-sugar smell.

name: Limoncello
description: The Italian lemon liqueur: sweet, sugary lemon peel with a boozy kick.
